rationale: Inverting the archive's maturity-wall design so that the *change* in near-term liability share becomes the primary predictor introduces a base variable not yet tested here, though the ratio can fall mechanically through long-term debt issuance (a known negative-return financing signal), which risks contaminating the intended sign, and the non-negative RANK conditioner only attenuates rather than flips the interaction.

GROWTH(cogs)−GROWTH(revt) is, to first order, the same construct as the already-tested DELTA(cogs/revt) margin squeeze and the gen-6 cost-stickiness triple, so this is a recombination of tested legs with a swapped liquidity conditioner rather than a new mechanism.

This is structurally the gen-5 "Profitable Net-Current-Debt Repair" signal with xint substituted for (dlc−che) as the improvement variable, and falling interest expense is largely a proxy for deleveraging/net-financing changes, a well-documented published anomaly rather than a novel cross-theme interaction.

This is a cosmetic variant of the gen-5 "Maturity-Wall Gross Profit Trend" winner — same TREND-of-profitability × RANK(dlc/lt) design with the lt/at leg dropped and the already-tested oibdp+xrd addback swapped in — offering little independent information.

This is close to the exact mirror of the gen-4 "Profitable Cash Rebuild Under Current Debt" signal (cash change × profitability rank × current-debt rank, all legs negated), which already produced a near-zero FF5 alpha, so the same information set is being re-sorted rather than extended.

The dp/at × profit-change × (dlc−che) triple has already been tested twice (gen 3 and gen 5) with sign-inconsistent results, and flipping DELTA to ACCEL and negating the direction reproduces the same variable set without diagnosing why the FMB slope and portfolio alpha previously disagreed.
